shipped_originals.title_o: At 6–9 months, human infants know the meanings of many common nouns

blind_target.title: The acquisition of abstract words by young infants.
blind_target.evidence_quote: This study confirms several patterns that have emerged in previous work ( Bergelson & Swingley, 2012 , 2013b ; Parise & Csibra, 2012 ; Tincoff & Jusczyk, 1999 , 2012 ). Namely, we find further evidence, with a new sample of infants and a new set of item pairs, that 6-9 month olds understand words.
blind_target.outcome_quote: While the study was not designed to test the difference between noun and verb acquisition, 6–9-month-olds did perform well on one of the two verb pairs ( hug - eat ), contrary to their poor performance on a broader set of non-nouns in a prior study ( Bergelson & Swingley, 2013 ). Whether infants’ apparent success on hug-eat represents random item variation, or a first fragile glimmer of infants’ understanding of these verbs, is unclear, particularly given infants’ failure to demonstrate understanding of kiss-drink here.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly contrast success on one verb pair with prior non-noun failure while another pair fails; they also confirm the age boost from this original. The broad sentence about confirming several patterns does not give an overall verdict on the entire replication of this paper. Agreement passage: Not unexpectedly, this ability increases with age, but perhaps less expectedly the rate with which it increases is non-linear. This is the third study that finds evidence of a boost in performance around 13-14 months, independent of word type ( Bergelson & Swingley, 2012 , 2013b ).

blind_target.title: Machine learning to analyze single-case graphs: A comparison to visual inspection.
blind_target.evidence_quote: A secondary purpose was to replicate and extend Lanovaz and Hranchuk (2021) by examining correspondence between visual inspection, the conservative dual-criteria method, and the machine-learning algorithms on a novel dataset.
blind_target.outcome_quote: In contrast, raters performed better on the clinical graphs than previously reported by Lanovaz and Hranchuk (2021) on simulated ones.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The discussion explicitly contrasts improved rater performance and the phase-length relation with this target; the predicted classifier agreement advantage was absent. No overall author verdict overrides these differences.

corrected_value.title: Machine learning to analyze single-case graphs: A comparison to visual inspection.

prior_decision.quote: A secondary purpose was to replicate and extend Lanovaz and Hranchuk (2021) by examining correspondence between visual inspection, the conservative dual-criteria method, and the machine-learning algorithms on a novel dataset. We extended both studies by using clinical data and adding a 10-point scale with definitional criteria to visual-inspection ratings.
prior_decision.reason: The authors explicitly define a secondary purpose as replicating Lanovaz and Hranchuk (2021) on new clinical data, distinct from the primary Wolfe et al. (2018) comparison. The reference identifies DOI 10.1002/jaba.863; the sole shipped pair is Wolfe (10.1002/jaba.453). Parent reviewed the cited results/purpose and reference identity against all supplied shipped originals. This decision confirms the missing paper-level pair only; its overall outcome has not been adjudicated.

blind_target.authors: Borreggine, K. L., & Kaschak, M. P.
blind_target.title: The action–sentence compatibility effect: It's all in the timing.
blind_target.evidence_quote: As a first step in assessing the replicability of motor compatibility effects, we conducted a pre-registered, multi-lab replication of the ACE. We used an adapted version of the original ACE paradigm (Glenberg & Kaschak, 2002) that was used in Borreggine and Kaschak (2006).
blind_target.outcome_quote: The results of the replication effort are clear: This version of the ACE was not statistically significant in any of the individual studies, and the meta-analytic effect size was close to zero (see Fig. 6).
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The overall verdict is a clear failure for this version of ACE in all 18 labs, with a near-zero pooled effect.
